findings.title: Dataclass default `queued` is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once, when the class is defined. Every AssignmentSource that doesn't pass `queued` gets the process start time, not the creation time. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued, so the value is misleading. It should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: to_dict returns a datetime that is not JSON-serializable for the task payload
findings.body: `asdict` leaves `queued` as a `datetime` object. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` passes this dict as a kwarg to `apply_async`. With a JSON serializer for Celery, this raises a serialization error or silently turns the value into a string. In that case `from_dict` later builds an AssignmentSource whose `queued` is a string. The datetime should be serialized explicitly, for example as an ISO string, and parsed back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: Subclass overrides of should_sync and sync_*_outbound may not accept the new args
findings.body: The task now calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and passes `assignment_source=` to `sync_assignee_outbound`. Integrations that override these methods with the old signature (for example a `should_sync(self, attribute)` override, or a `sync_assignee_outbound` without `**kwargs`) will raise TypeError. The abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` accepts `**kwargs`, but `sync_status_outbound` callers and other overrides were not audited in this PR.
